paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “It is widely accepted that an important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，您有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“人们普遍认为教育的一个重要目标是帮助学生学会如何学习。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists recently examined studies on dog intelligence and compared them with research into the minds of other intelligent animals. The researchers found that dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores (食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals, but that their intelligence does not 26 other intelligent animals in any of those categories. Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition 27 , the authors of this new study found little to warrant the 28 of work that has been devoted to the topic.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家最近检查了有关狗智力的研究，并将其与对其他聪明动物的思想的研究进行了比较。研究人员发现，狗是最聪明的食肉动物、群居猎手和家养动物之一，但它们的智力并没有超过任何这些类别中的其他聪明动物。尽管之前有大量研究考察了狗的认知能力，但这项新研究的作者发现，没有什么值得专门研究该主题的工作量。

paragraphs.sourceText: Stephen Lea, lead author of the new study, argues that many researchers seem to have designed their studies to 29 how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs’ brains. Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition, comparing the studies’ results with those from research into other animals. The researchers made specific comparisons between the different species in different categories of intelligence. These comparisons 30 that dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as 31 as some researchers might have believed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项新研究的主要作者斯蒂芬·李（Stephen Lea）认为，许多研究人员设计他们的研究似乎是为了证明狗有多么聪明，而不仅仅是为了研究狗的大脑。 Lea 和一位同事检查了 300 多项关于狗认知的研究，并将这些研究的结果与其他动物的研究结果进行了比较。研究人员对不同物种的不同智力类别进行了具体比较。这些比较证实了狗是聪明的，但它们的智力并不像一些研究人员想象的那么强大。

paragraphs.sourceText: In many areas, though, comparisons were not possible. For example, the researchers noted that both dogs and cats are known to be able to recognize and 32 human voices. But the investigators could not find any data to indicate which species can remember a greater number of 33 human voices, so it was impossible to compare the two on that front. However, not all researchers agree 34 with the findings of this study. Zachary Silver, an American researcher, believes the authors of the new study 35 the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young, and there is much to be learned about how dogs think.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但在许多领域，无法进行比较。例如，研究人员指出，众所周知，狗和猫都能够识别和区分人类的声音。但研究人员无法找到任何数据来表明哪个物种可以记住更多数量的不同人类声音，因此不可能在这方面对两者进行比较。然而，并非所有研究人员完全同意这项研究的结果。美国研究人员扎卡里·西尔弗（Zachary Silver）认为，这项新研究的作者夸大了对狗进行了大量研究的观点，因为狗的认知领域还很年轻，关于狗的思维方式还有很多东西需要了解。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Lifesaving Power of Gratitude
paragraphs.translationZh: 感恩的拯救生命的力量

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose. One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel — an impact that they consistently underestimated. Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes. The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduced symptoms of depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 感恩可能比我们通常想象的更有益。最近的一项研究要求参与者写一封感谢信，然后估计收件人会感到多么惊讶和高兴——他们一直低估了这种影响。另一项研究评估了写感谢信对健康的好处。研究人员发现，在三周的时间内每周写三封感谢信可以提高生活满意度，增加幸福感并减少抑郁症状。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe’s 300-year-old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English. Left alone on an unknown island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament (悲叹). But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck (海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 虽然这项关于感恩的研究相对较新，但所涉及的原则却绝非如此。我在印第安纳大学修读政治哲学课程的学生正在阅读丹尼尔·笛福 (Daniel Defoe) 300 年前的《鲁滨逊漂流记》，这本书通常被认为是第一本英文出版的小说。克鲁索被独自留在一个不知名的岛屿上，没有明显的获救或逃脱的希望，他有很多悲叹。但他没有屈服于绝望，而是列出了他感激的事情，包括他是海难中唯一的幸存者，并且能够从残骸中打捞出许多有用的物品。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Defoe’s masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world’s greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been. It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up. Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 笛福的这部杰作经常被评为世界上最伟大的小说之一，它描绘了感恩的行动，在今天仍然像以往一样及时和相关。当代心理学和医学也刚刚开始追赶这一趋势。简而言之，对于我们大多数人来说，关注生活中那些我们可以表达感激的事情比那些让我们怨恨和哀叹的事情更有帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives. And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 当我们专注于那些让我们后悔的事情时，比如失败的人际关系、家庭纠纷、事业和财务方面的挫折，我们往往会变得更加后悔。相反，当我们专注于我们感激的事情时，更大的幸福感往往会在我们的生活中蔓延。虽然没有人会主张培养一种错误的幸福感，但越来越多的证据表明，数算我们的幸福是我们可以养成的促进身心健康的最佳习惯之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world’s cultural traditions. For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 感恩长期以来在世界许多文化传统中享有特权地位。例如，一些古代西方哲学家主张感恩是持久而完整的，而一些东方思想家则将其描述为不仅是一种态度，而且是一种需要付诸实践的美德。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness. And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. They may also be moral — those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 最近的科学研究支持这些古老的教义。经常进行感恩练习的人，例如计算自己的祝福或向他人表达感激之情，会对人际关系表现出更高的满意度，并减少身体疾病的症状。而且好处不仅是心理上和身体上的。他们也可能是有道德的——那些懂得感恩的人也不会那么物质化地看待自己的生活，也不会受到太多的嫉妒。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness. One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate (回报) with acts of kindness of their own. Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity. Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 对于感恩的这种好处有多种解释。一是表达感激之情会鼓励他人继续慷慨，从而促进人际关系的良性循环。同样，心存感激的人可能更有可能以自己的善举来回报。一般来说，一个人们彼此感激的社区可能比一个相互猜疑和怨恨的社区更令人愉快。感恩的有益影响可能会进一步扩大。例如，当许多人对其他人为他们所做的事情感到满意时，他们会体验到一种被提升的感觉，相应地也会增强他们对人性的尊重。有些人受到启发，尝试让自己成为更好的人，做更多的事情来帮助他人发挥出最好的一面，并为周围的世界带来更多的善良。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 感恩也往往会加强与他人的联系感。当人们想做一些能激发感激之情的好事时，人际关系中的奉献程度往往会提高，关系似乎会持续更长时间。当人们感觉联系更紧密时，他们更有可能选择与彼此共度时光，并在日常行为中表达他们的感情。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior (别有用心的) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized. Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received. Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so. Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement. Instead of experiencing a benefaction (善行) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 当然，善意的行为也会引起不适。例如，如果人们觉得自己不值得仁慈，或者怀疑其背后有别有用心的动机，那么感恩的好处就不会实现。同样，接受善意可能会产生一种负债感，让受益人觉得他们现在必须偿还他们所收到的任何善意。只有当人们对自己有足够的安全感和足够的信任时，感恩之心才能蓬勃发展。感恩的另一个障碍通常被称为权利感。人们有时并不把善行视为一种善行，而是仅仅将其视为对自己所欠之物的偿还，没有人值得为此获得任何道德信誉。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) There are a number of practical steps anyone can take to promote a sense of gratitude. One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person. Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor. In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future. Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others. In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe’s Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 任何人都可以采取许多实际步骤来增强感恩感。一种是定期花时间思考那些做出了贡献的人，或者写一封感谢信或当面表达这种感激之情。其他的则存在于古代宗教戒律中，例如反思从他人那里收到的善行或实际祈祷捐助者的健康和幸福。除了收到的善意之外，还可以关注为自己做好事的机会，无论是过去做过的还是未来希望得到的。有些人最感激的不是别人为他们所做的事情，而是他们有机会帮助别人。笛福笔下的克鲁索经常反思自己生活中值得感激的事情，他相信，如果他留在最初出海的社会中，他会成为一个更好的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students. First, he said, “It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you.” In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. Second, he said, “Give thanks for your blessings every day.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 伟大的篮球教练约翰·伍登（John Wooden）出于慷慨和感激之情，曾向他的球员和学生提出两条忠告。首先，他说，“除非你为永远无法回报你的人做了一些事情，否则你不可能拥有完美的一天。”在这么说时，伍登试图提倡纯粹的慷慨行为，而不是那些期望获得回报的行为。其次，他说：“感谢你每天的祝福。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life. For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep. Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals. Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 一些信仰传统将这种做法融入日常生活的节奏中。例如，一些宗教的信徒每天早上起床前和每天晚上睡觉前都会进行感恩祈祷。其他人全天表示感谢，例如饭前。其他不太常见的特殊事件，例如出生、死亡和婚姻，也可能通过这种祈祷来预示。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years. Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years. Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）当笛福描绘鲁宾逊漂流记将感恩节作为他岛上生活的日常一部分时，他期待着社会科学和医学方面的发现，而这些发现在数百年后才会出现。然而，他也反映了几千年前宗教和哲学传统的智慧。感恩是所有心态中最健康、最滋养的一种，那些将感恩作为一种习惯的人不仅丰富了自己的生活，也丰富了周围人的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It does us far more good to focus on things we can be grateful for than what makes us sad and resentful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 关注那些让我们感激的事情比关注让我们悲伤和怨恨的事情对我们更有好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The beneficial impacts of gratitude can extend from individuals to their community and to the wider society.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 感恩的有益影响可以从个人延伸到社区和更广泛的社会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The participants in a recent study repeatedly underestimated the positive effect on those who received thank-you notes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 最近一项研究的参与者一再低估了对那些收到感谢信的人的积极影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Good deeds can sometimes make people feel uncomfortable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39、做好事有时会让人感到不舒服。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. People who regularly express gratitude can benefit in moral terms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 经常表达感激之情的人可以在道德上受益。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. A basketball coach advocated performing generous acts without expecting anything in return.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一位篮球教练主张做出慷慨的行为而不求任何回报。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. More and more evidence shows it makes us mentally and physically healthier to routinely count our blessings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 越来越多的证据表明，经常数算我们的祝福可以让我们的身心更加健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Of all states of mind, feeling grateful is considered one of the most healthy and beneficial.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 在所有心态中，感恩被认为是最健康、最有益的心态之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The principles underlying the research into gratitude are nothing new at all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 感恩研究的基本原则并不是什么新鲜事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Gratitude is likely to enhance one’s sense of being connected with other people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 感恩可能会增强一个人与他人的联系感。

For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 技术从来都不是实现人类目标的中立工具。技术创新重塑了人们，因为他们利用这些创新来控制他们的环境。例如，人工智能正在改变人类。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human? Central to the problem is a person’s capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然人工智能一词让人联想到杀手机器人或灾难性失业水平的焦虑，但还有其他更深层次的影响。随着人工智能日益塑造人类体验，这将如何改变人类的意义？问题的核心是一个人做出选择的能力，尤其是做出具有道德影响的判断的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them — on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 亚里士多德认为，做出实际判断的能力取决于定期做出判断——习惯和实践。我们认为机器在各种日常环境中作为替代法官的出现对人们学习如何有效地运用判断本身构成了潜在威胁。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where algorithmic (算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在工作场所，经理们通常会决定雇用或解雇谁以及批准哪些贷款等等。在这些领域，算法处方正在取代人类判断，因此那些原本有机会在这些领域培养实际判断力的人将不再有机会了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people’s consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.
paragraphs.translationZh: 推荐引擎作为人们文化消费中越来越普遍的中介，可能会限制选择并减少运气。通过向消费者提供由算法选择的下一步观看、阅读、流媒体和访问内容的选择，公司正在用机器品味取代人类品味。从某种意义上说，这是有帮助的。毕竟，机器可以调查的选择范围比任何个人可能有时间或精力自己做的选择范围更广。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they’ve preferred in the past. We think there is some risk that people’s options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但与此同时，这种选择是根据人们过去的偏好来优化他们可能喜欢的内容。我们认为，人们的选择可能会以一种新的、意想不到的方式受到过去的限制。

paragraphs.sourceText: As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着机器学习算法的改进以及在更广泛的数据集上进行训练，日常生活的大部分内容可能会变得完全可预测。预测将会变得越来越好，最终将使共同的体验变得更加高效和愉快。

paragraphs.sourceText: Algorithms could soon — if they don’t already — have a better idea about which show you’d like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display.
paragraphs.translationZh: 算法很快就会（如果还没有的话）比你更好地了解你接下来想看哪个节目以及你应该雇用哪位求职者。有一天，人类甚至可能找到一种方法让机器做出这些决定，而不会出现人类通常表现出的一些偏见。

paragraphs.sourceText: But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但在某种程度上，不可预测性是人们如何理解自己的一部分，也是人们对自己的喜好的一部分，人类正在失去一些重要的东西。随着它们变得越来越可预测，居住在日益人工智能介导的世界中的生物将变得越来越不像我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Phonics, which involves sounding out words syllable (音节) by syllable, is the best way to teach children to read. But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. Most American children are taught to read in a way that study after study has found to be wrong.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自然拼读法（Phonics）涉及一个音节一个音节地发音，是教孩子阅读的最佳方法。但在许多教室里，这可能是一个肮脏的词。以至于一些老师不得不将自然拼读教材偷偷带进课堂。大多数美国孩子所接受的阅读教育方式都被多次研究发现是错误的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The consequences of this are striking. Less than half of all American adults were proficient readers in 2017. American fourth graders rank 15th on the Progress in International Literacy Study, an international exam.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其后果是惊人的。 2017 年，只有不到一半的美国成年人能够熟练阅读。美国四年级学生在国际读写能力研究进展国际考试中排名第 15 位。

paragraphs.sourceText: America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as “whole language”. Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the EdWeek Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called “balanced literacy”. This combination of methods is ineffective. “You can’t sprinkle in a little phonics,” says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi’s education department. “It has to be systematic and explicitly taught.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国陷入了一场持续了数十年的关于教孩子阅读的争论。有些人主张教授符号与声音的关系（声音 k 可以拼写为 c、k、ck 或 ch），称为自然拼读法。其他人支持沉浸式方法（使用猫的图片来学习猫这个词），称为“完整语言”。根据 EdWeek 研究中心 2019 年的一项调查，当今大多数教师（几乎四分之三）都使用一种称为“平衡读写能力”的组合。这种方法的组合是无效的。 “你不能加入一点自然拼读法，”密西西比州教育部门基础教育和阅读执行主任特内特·史密斯 (Tenette Smith) 说。 “它必须系统化、明确地教授。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi’s pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state.
paragraphs.translationZh: 经常在社会政策方面落后的密西西比州在这里树立了榜样。密西西比州曾经因阅读成绩低而臭名昭著，但它于 2013 年通过了新的识字标准。自那时起，密西西比州取得了显着的进步。该州四年级学生在全国教育进步评估考试中的排名从第 49 位（在 50 个州中）上升至第 29 位。 2019年，它是唯一一个得分提高的州。自测量开始以来，密西西比州的学生第一次达到了平均阅读水平，在如此贫穷的州，这是一项了不起的成就。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mississippi’s success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading. In 1997 Congress requested the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the Department of Education to convene a National Reading Panel to end the “reading wars” and synthesize the evidence. The panel found that phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic (音位的) awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best.
paragraphs.translationZh: 密西西比州的成功归功于实施由阅读科学研究机构支持的阅读方法。 1997年，国会要求国家儿童健康和人类发展研究所和教育部召开全国阅读小组会议，以结束“阅读大战”并综合证据。小组发现，自然拼读法以及对音位意识、流畅性和理解力的明确指导效果最好。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yet over two decades on, “balanced literacy” is still being taught in classrooms. But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method. To the teacher who is a proficient reader, literacy seems like a natural process that requires educated guessing, rather than the deliberate process emphasized by phonics. Teachers can imagine that they learned to read through osmosis (潜移默化) when they were children. Without proper training, they bring this to classrooms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而二十多年来，“平衡识字”仍在课堂上教授。但统计学和脑成像技术的进步已经推翻了全语言方法。对于精通阅读的老师来说，识字似乎是一个自然的过程，需要有根据的猜测，而不是拼读法强调的刻意过程。老师们可以想象，他们小时候是通过潜移默化学会了阅读。如果没有经过适当的培训，他们就会将其带到课堂上。

paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 在许多美国课堂上我们学到了什么有关自然拼读的知识？

paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 几十年来美国目睹了什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 53.为什么特内特·史密斯认为多种教学方法的组合是无效的？
